title: A scope file: the target a hunt may reach, who owns it, and how much the hunt may send (kamanu hunt --scope, card R14d)
description: Every hunt entry point reads this before its first request and refuses (exit 6, kamanu.hunt.scope.ScopeRefused) without one that covers the adapter's real target. A scope covers a target when the two are equal, string for string. What the schema cannot say (expires is a real calendar date and has not passed, UTC) kamanu.hunt.scope checks. Extra keys are allowed at the top level only.

target.description: what the adapter will reach: the adapter's name and exactly one of an address, a binary path or a gateway id

adapter.description: the adapter's name, as its engine declares it (dogwood, dogwood-local, kong, litellm, redis-sliding-log, python-limits, agentcore)

address.description: a network address, as the adapter is given it

binary.description: a binary's path, as the adapter is given it (dogwood: the path DOGWOOD_BIN names)

basis.description: why the hunt may reach the target: it is the owner's own instance, or the owner published a statement that puts it in scope

ceilings.description: the most the hunt may send; the hunt counts both and stops before the request that would pass either

money.description: the most money, in the engine's unit: the sum of the amounts the requests ask for, whatever the engine answers

expires.description: the last day (UTC) the scope holds, YYYY-MM-DD
